bullets.title: LITE: Optical components completely sold out through early 2029; AI server demand surges
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO confirmed AI server optical components are completely sold out through early 2029 (extended from prior 2028 guidance), unable to meet ~70% of demand for some products through next year. Stock hit 52-week highs with +567% YTD gain. Competitor AAOI, COHR, CIEN, FN, and GLW all rallied in sympathy.

bullets.title: MRVL: Investor Day sharply raises targets—FY28 $20B, FY31 $70-90B revenue; stock +8%
bullets.body: Marvell's Investor Day raised FY28 revenue guidance from ~$18B to $20B and introduced FY31 framework of $70–90B revenue (55–60% CAGR) with >$30 EPS. Custom silicon target raised to $12B+ in FY29; interconnect TAM to $37.5B. Sell-side consensus raised PTs ~13% to avg $337 with 90% buy ratings. TD Cowen and others upgraded to buy.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro orders cut 15-20% on weak demand; first consumer demand hit from price hikes
bullets.body: Apple instructed suppliers to cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by at least 15% in October due to softer-than-expected demand following ~$100 price increases. KeyBanc estimates ~52.8M F4Q units vs consensus 57.8M. SWKS (~60% AAPL revenue exposure) and QRVO at risk. PC shipments also fell 20.1% YoY in 3Q26 with Apple gaining share despite declines.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini Agent launch, nuclear deal with CEG, Muse competition signals active week
bullets.body: Google launched Gemini Agent for enterprise with multi-model orchestration (including Claude). Separately, CEG confirmed a 20-year 890MW new nuclear deal with Google plus a 15-year 2.7GW existing capacity PPA in PJM—an estimated $2.50/share EPS uplift for CEG. Google also bid $1B+ in nuclear power and signed a 3.6GW deal with CEG total. Privacy concerns emerged over Google's acquisition of Spirit Airlines data for AI training.

bullets.title: SpaceX $8B 800MHz spectrum deal hammers VZ/T/TMUS; towers rally
bullets.body: SpaceX acquired nationwide 800MHz low-band spectrum from Grain Management for ~$8B, positioning Starlink Mobile as a potential 4th US wireless carrier. T, VZ, TMUS fell 6-10% with heavy put activity. Tower stocks (AMT, CCI, SBAC) rallied 7-12% on expected new colocation demand. Citi sizes 21%/20%/10% upside for CCI/SBAC/AMT respectively. Analysts split on near-term competitive threat timeline.

bullets.title: META: Muse #1 US app for 22 consecutive days; $27B+ revenue potential, agentic commerce threat
bullets.body: Meta's Muse AI agent remained #1 US App Store download for 22 consecutive days with 6.6M+ downloads and 1.8M DAUs. Citi raised META to Buy with $800 PT modeling $27B+ long-term revenue via transaction monetization. OTA stocks (EXPE, BKNG, ABNB) fell 15-25% on commission pool disruption fears, though Wolfe views marketplace selloff as overdone. Amazon blocked Muse from its platform.

bullets.title: NFLX: Preparing 5% workforce RIF (~850 employees); MS maintains OW at $80 PT
bullets.body: Netflix is preparing a restructuring announcement as early as next week affecting approximately 5% of employees (~850 workers), per Puck News. Separately, Morgan Stanley reiterated Overweight with PT cut from $83 to $80 on FX headwinds, citing double-digit revenue growth and 150-200bps margin expansion at ~15x FY28 EPS as undervalued. Ad revenue projected to triple from ~$1.6B (2025) to $4.8B (2027).

bullets.title: TSM: September revenue +55% YoY; record quarterly revenue; capex raised to $85B/yr in 2027
bullets.body: TSMC September revenue rose ~55% YoY to nearly NT$500B, beating expectations on unrelenting AI chip demand. FY26 capex guidance raised to $60-64B; UBS raised 2027-28 estimates with capex expected $85B/$98B. TSMC also explored a second US fab cluster in Texas (potential $265B+ investment) with Tesla/SpaceX anchor. Separately, TSMC confirmed strong N2 ramp timing with N3 capacity still tight.

bullets.title: ANET: Scale-Up Etherlink SU-144 unlocks $10B TAM; Citi initiates Buy at $248
bullets.body: Arista launched Etherlink SU-144, a pure Ethernet-based scale-up networking solution competing with NVDA's NVLink and UALink. The ESUN (Ethernet for Scale-Up) standard is imminent with an estimated $10B TAM in 2027. Microsoft is collaborating on Maia accelerators and META on scale-out. Citi initiates Buy at $248 (17.6% upside, 36x 2028 EPS).

bullets.title: ACN: +7% on PERM visa suspension; Buy-rated at $275 PT ahead of Analyst Day
bullets.body: Accenture surged ~5-6% after the Trump administration suspended multiple tech firms from the H-1B PERM green card program (including MSFT, ADBE, CTSH), with the market interpreting this as reducing offshore IT competition. UBS maintains Buy at $275 PT ahead of the Oct 14 Analyst Day, which is expected to clarify FY27+ long-term growth with $8B in FY27 M&A. Separately, ACN launched Dell Business Group for agentic AI workloads.

bullets.title: PLTR: Goldman upgrades to Buy at $230 PT on sovereign AI TAM step-change
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral, raising the PT to $230 (18% upside), citing a step-function change in TAM through sovereign AI and verticalization strategy. PLTR's FDE model with AI automation sustains competitive advantage; revenue estimates raised meaningfully from 2027 onward. Stock had lagged high-growth peers (SNOW/NET/DDOG up 50-100% YTD vs PLTR +9% YTD pre-upgrade).

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM raises PT to $200 on ~30% 2027 revenue growth and agentic commerce positioning
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised Shopify's December 2027 price target from $185 to $200 (23x 2028E gross profit), reiterating as top pick and Analyst Focus List name. SHOP delivered five consecutive quarters of 30%+ GMV and revenue growth. AI-driven retail traffic converts at ~2x vs traditional channels; Shop Pay integrated into Meta Muse and OpenAI ChatGPT. Agentic commerce positioned to drive further upside.

bullets.title: MU: Strong Q4 results; tight supply through CY28; imminent buyback pivot
bullets.body: Micron reported record Q4 revenue with profit up over 1000%; 75% of 2027 output already allocated. CY27-28 supply significantly tighter than CY26 with demand growth above industry supply. HBM pricing expected to roughly double from HBM3E to HBM4. MU and Netlist settled patent dispute with $600M payment (five-year, $30M/quarter). DA Davidson raised PT to $3,000. MU Taiwan union authorized strike over bonus dispute (potential supply risk).

bullets.title: HUT: River Bend on time/budget; WULF expands Muskie to 1GW—PSP top picks in AI infra
bullets.body: HUT's River Bend Phase 1 (330MW/245MW IT) is on schedule with ~1,100 workers; first 65MW IT expected online 2Q27. WULF finalized expanded Kentucky Power electricity contract (1GW contracted, second 500MW delivery moved to 2029). UBS $143 PT and ROTH $108 PT on HUT; Morgan Stanley updated Powered Shell Provider yields from 15% to 19%. Both stocks cited as top picks in AI data center infrastructure.

bullets.title: AMD: Raises 2027 supply substantially; Citi PT to $800 on agentic CPU TAM expansion
bullets.body: AMD CEO announced plans to substantially increase chip supply in 2027 to meet 'very high' AI demand, including exploring Samsung foundry partnership. Citi raised AMD PT to $800 citing Meta Muse agentic AI driving CPU TAM expansion from $29B (2025) to $300B (2030) at 60% CAGR. AMD is identified as primary CPU beneficiary as Meta is one of largest AMD server customers.

bullets.title: NOW: Partner call shows strong AI SKU adoption with 10-25% spend uplift; 2027 visibility solid
bullets.body: JPMorgan's elite-tier ServiceNow partner call revealed all renewing customers are migrating to new AI SKUs with 10-25% average spend uplift. Q3 landed on plan; Q4 tracking 35-40% of annual bookings. Partner expects 2027 growth better than 2026 on new SKUs and consumption revenue. Flow product sees no enterprise-level competitors; AI Control Tower gaining governance traction.

bullets.title: SNOW: Chicago conference shows CoCo adoption at 50% of customers; FQ3 above plan
bullets.body: KeyBanc's Snowflake Chicago conference survey found 50% of customers actively using Cortex Code (up from 6% prior quarter); 40%+ report FQ3 consumption trending above expectations vs 30% prior. 9 of 10 CoCo users report bill increases with no near-term plans to limit spend. CEO framed cycle as 'industrializing intelligence.' PT $460 based on 18x FY29E EV/revenue.

bullets.title: HD/LOW: UBS survey shows home improvement demand at 2-year high; professional engagement up
bullets.body: UBS Evidence Lab survey of 61% of homeowners planning projects in the next 12 months—highest in 2+ years and above the 57% historical average. Home Depot maintains 53% primary destination preference vs Lowe's 38%. Professional hiring intent rose 250bps YoY. Paint project planners citing HD rose significantly. Flooring project interest improved to ~21% from ~17-18%, suggesting higher-ticket willingness.

bullets.title: HUBS: 7% workforce RIF announced; downgraded by JPM/Raymond James on AI monetization delays
bullets.body: HubSpot disclosed a restructuring plan eliminating ~7% of workforce (~660 employees) with $65-75M in charges; Q3 and FY26 guidance reaffirmed and FY30 operating margin target raised to 30%. However, JPMorgan downgraded HUBS to Neutral (PT $240 from $268) citing delayed AI monetization vs expectations, and Raymond James also downgraded. Market reaction was muted as investors focus on revenue reacceleration.

bullets.title: CEG: Google nuclear PPA (+$2.50/share EPS); IPP sector rallied ~15% on AI power deals
bullets.body: Constellation Energy confirmed a 20-year 890MW new nuclear + 15-year 2.7GW existing capacity agreement with Google, representing $4.3B+ in new investment. IPPs rallied ~15% on average as data center power is increasingly viewed as real and monetizable. VST and TLN also gained on sentiment that data center PPAs are achievable without 1-for-1 new generation requirements in PJM.
